aliases: reflection of a category in a subcategory

evidence.intree_statement: Record Reflective {C : Category} (S : Subcategory C) := { reflective_full : Construction.Subcategory.Full C S; reflector : C ⟶ Sub C S; reflective_adj : reflector ⊣ Incl C S }.

statement_record.book: A subcategory A of B is reflective when the inclusion K : A -> B has a left adjoint F (the reflector); the adjunction <F, K, phi> is a reflection of B in A. Equivalent descriptions: a functor R : B -> B with values in A and a natural bijection A(Rb, a) ≅ B(b, a); or, for each b, a universal arrow eta_b : b -> Rb to the subcategory.
statement_record.intree: Record Reflective bundles fullness of the subcategory, the reflector C ⟶ Sub C S, and the adjunction reflector ⊣ Incl C S (Construction/Reflective.v:60-64), over Construction/Subcategory.v's Sub/Incl.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-stronger (narrower): the record additionally demands fullness of the subcategory, whereas Mac Lane defines reflectivity for an arbitrary subcategory and treats fullness as a separate condition (his remark2 covers the full case); this matches the modern nLab convention. Mac Lane's two equivalent reformulations (the R : B -> B natural-bijection form and the universal-arrow form) are not separately proven, though the universal-arrow form is recoverable from the general adjunction ⟺ universal-arrows machinery of Theory/Universal/Arrow.v

evidence.intree_statement: Lemma reflective_counit_iso {C : Category} {S : Subcategory C} (R : Reflective S) (x : Sub C S) : reflector R (Incl C S x) ≅[Sub C S] x.
Lemma reflective_counit_IsIso (x : Sub C S) : IsIsomorphism (@counit (Sub C S) C (reflector R) (Incl C S) (reflective_adj R) x).

statement_record.book: If a full subcategory A of B is reflective, then each a in A is isomorphic to FKa (by Theorem IV.3.1), hence Ra ≅ a for all a in A: the reflector restricted to A is naturally isomorphic to the identity.
statement_record.intree: For any Reflective S (fullness is a record field), the counit component at each subcategory object x is an isomorphism reflector R (Incl C S x) ≅ x, with the counit as forward map and the fullness-lifted unit as inverse; proved from the two triangle identities plus counit naturality.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same: the componentwise counit iso is exactly Mac Lane's Ra ≅ a (the iso even lives in Sub C S, which via the full inclusion agrees with an iso in the ambient category); the in-tree proof is direct from the triangle identities rather than a corollary of the (absent) Theorem IV.3.1, a presentation difference only. The bundling into a natural isomorphism reflector ∘ Incl ≅ Id is not stated as such but the componentwise form is what Mac Lane asserts
